title: They Left Home With Shillings, Bought Pies With a £5 Note... Where Did It Come From?
description:
On Australia Day 1966, Jane (9), Arnna (7), and Grant Beaumont (4) caught the bus alone to Glenelg Beach in Adelaide — a completely normal errand for the era. When they didn't return on the expected buses, their mother's worry turned to panic. Witnesses recalled a tall, tanned, blond stranger with the children that morning, and a baker confirmed selling them meat pies paid for with a crisp five-pound note — despite the kids leaving home with only a few shillings.

What followed became the largest search in South Australian history, yielding nothing. Decades of false leads, disputed handwriting on letters claiming to be from Jane, and a 2013 excavation of a North Plympton factory floor tied to a suspect who'd already been dead for years — all turned up empty. No bodies. No arrest. No closure.

Fifty-eight years later, the Beaumont children case remains one of Australia's most haunting unsolved mysteries — and nobody has ever explained where that five-pound note came from.
